note: Hook and loop shapes for the best-of-N writer (pipeline/bestof.py, user 2026-11-15). A shape is filled from the episode's twist fact; the examples show the shape on other topics and are never copied. A hook may only argue against a belief people really hold (the topic's misconception or claims).

hooks.how: name the common belief, then hint it is wrong
hooks.example: You were told sugar makes kids hyper.

hooks.how: say a familiar idea is usually misunderstood
hooks.example: Almost everyone gets this about lightning wrong.

hooks.how: compare the subject's age with something famous
hooks.example: Your salt is older than the dinosaurs.

hooks.shape: Something you use every day hides X
hooks.how: connect an everyday object to the surprise
hooks.example: Your toothpaste hides a sea fossil.

hooks.how: flip the belief in two short sentences, no answer given away in full
hooks.example: It's not the cold. It's the dry air.

hooks.how: lead with a true, striking number from the research
hooks.example: One teaspoon holds a billion bacteria.

hooks.how: ask what the viewer would lose or miss
hooks.example: What if your coffee is older than you think?

hooks.how: contrast what it was with what it became
hooks.example: It was sunlight. Now it's in your tank.

hooks.how: ask for the true source in plain words
hooks.example: What really makes a rainbow?

hooks.how: drop the viewer into a scene from the story
hooks.example: Picture a sea with no fish at all.

hooks.how: contrast scale
hooks.example: Something smaller than dust built the cliffs of Dover.

hooks.how: send the viewer to the time the story starts
hooks.example: Go back 300 million years.

hooks.how: the viewer is touching the subject without knowing
hooks.example: You're holding ancient starlight right now.

hooks.how: name the myth in a short label
hooks.example: The five-second-rule myth.

hooks.how: tease the real ingredient without naming it
hooks.example: The secret ingredient isn't what you think.

hooks.how: voice the viewer's surprise
hooks.example: Wait, glass is still a solid?

hooks.how: a mystery with no witness, solved by evidence
hooks.example: Nobody saw the Grand Canyon form.

hooks.how: promise a one-word answer the payoff gives
hooks.example: One word explains every sunset.

hooks.shape: If you think X, watch this
hooks.how: address the viewer who holds the belief
hooks.example: If you think bats are blind, watch this.

hooks.how: say what believing the myth gets wrong
hooks.example: Believing this wastes your sunscreen.

hooks.shape: The real reason, not the famous one
hooks.how: contrast the famous answer with the real one
hooks.example: The famous reason is wrong. Here's the real one.

hooks.how: admit the fact sounds impossible
hooks.example: This sounds wrong, but ice can burn.

hooks.how: trace an everyday thing back to its origin
hooks.example: Your chalk came from tiny sea shells.

hooks.shape: In one second / in one lifetime
hooks.how: a time-scale contrast
hooks.example: It took longer than all of human history.

hooks.how: frame the story as a search for who did it
hooks.example: Let's find who really made the desert.

loops.shape: Next time you X, remember Y
loops.how: tie an everyday action back to the hook
loops.example: Next time you salt your fries, think of that sea.

loops.how: repeat the hook's words and answer them in a few words
loops.example: So, what makes a rainbow? Raindrops.

loops.shape: An open question for the comments
loops.how: ask something the viewer can answer below, using a hook word
loops.example: What else do you think is older than the dinosaurs?

loops.how: return to the opening image with the new meaning
loops.example: That puddle? Now you know what's in it.

loops.shape: It was never X. It was Y.
loops.how: restate the twist as the final word, using a hook word
loops.example: It was never the cold. It was the air.

loops.how: hand the viewer the new fact to share
loops.example: Now you know why the sky is blue.

loops.shape: All of that, in one X
loops.how: compress the story into one object
loops.example: All of that, in one grain of sand.

loops.shape: Tell the friend who believes X
loops.how: send the viewer to correct the myth
loops.example: Tell the friend who swears bats are blind.

loops.how: say the process goes on today (only if the research says so)
loops.example: And it's still happening on the sea floor today.

loops.how: end on the hook's key word, now with a new meaning

loops.shape: Which is why the hook is true
loops.how: the last line makes the first line make sense on rewatch
loops.example: Which is why your salt is older than the dinosaurs.

loops.how: invite a rewatch of the first frame
loops.example: Look again at that first drop.
